texts.preamble: Sukhdev Sharma vs Kakpil Dev Sharma And Ors on 27 February, 2024 In The Court Of Ms. Anuradha Jindal, Administrative Civil Judge-Cum-Commercial Cases Judge-Cum-Additional Rent Controller, South West District, Dwarka Courts, New Delhi Cnr No. : Dlsw03-001230-2016 Sukhdev Sharma v. Kapil Dev & Anr. a) Case No. : 27314/2016 b) Name & address of the : 1. Sukhdev Sharma, plaintiff S/o Late Sh. Munshi Ram Sharma R/o A-1/9, A-1 Block, Vijay Enclave, New Delhi 110045 c) Name & address of the : 1.Shri Kapil Dev Sharma defendant S/o Shri Sukhdev Sharma R/o Plot No. 127, Point B, Top Floor, Near Mother Dairy, Bagdola, Sector 8, Dwarka, New Delhi 110075 2. Smt. Ritu Sharma W/o Shri Kapil Dev Sharma, R/o A-1/9, A-1 Block, Vijay Enclave, New Delhi 110045 Date of Institution of petition : 14.09.2016 Date of pronouncement of judgment : 27.02.2024 Csscj/27314/2016 Sukhdev Sharma v. Kapil Dev Sharma & Ors. Page 1/50 Judgment 1 The Case 1.1.
texts.facts: The present suit relates to a case wherein the father-in- law/plaintiff seeks permanent injunction against the son/ defendant no. 1 thereby restraining him from entering the suit property shown green in the site plan and mandatory injunction against daughter-in-law/defendant no. 2 thereby directing her to vacate the suit property and remove her articles/belongings from portion shown red in the site plan and remove all/other articles, if any, from suit property shown green in the site plan. 1.3. The plaintiff has instituted the present suit for the following reliefs: "A. "Pass a decree of mandatory injunction thereby directing defendant no. 2 to vacate suit property bearing No. A-1/9, A-1 BLOCK, VIJAY ENCLAVE, NEW DELHI-110045, and remove her articles/belongings from portion shown red in the site plan and remove all/other articles, if any, from suit property shown green in the site plan, in the interest of justice. B. Pass a decree of permanent injunction thereby restraining defendant No. 1 from entering the suit property shown green in the site plan, for any reason whatsoever, in the interest of justice. Pleaded case of the plaintiff is that plaintiff is the owner and in possession of the suit property. The suit property was originally purchased by one Sh. Kartar Singh from Sh. Kehri through his attorney Sh. Mahavir Singh, vide title documents dated 20.09.1985. The plaintiff purchased the suit property from Sh. Kartar Singh vide title documents dated 20.11.1986 for valid consideration. Post marriage, defendant no. 1 and defendant no. 2, were allowed by plaintiff to live in his house i.e., suit property, in view of relationship between plaintiff and defendants. However, at no point of time, the ownership or exclusive possession of suit property, or any portion thereof, was ever transferred to any of the defendants by plaintiff. 2.2. The plaintiff is residing in the suit property alongwith his wife. In front portion of the suit property, plaintiff is carrying on business of Dwarka Sweets and Caterers and Chaar Yaar restaurant. After a certain period of time, plaintiff asked defendants to arrange their separate residential accommodation but defendants lingered on the issue on one pretext or the other. In January 2014, when plaintiff asked defendants to vacate the suit property, defendant no. 2 started quarreling with plaintiff and his wife. Thereafter, plaintiff asked the defendants to vacate the suit property number of times but to no avail. On the contrary, defendant no.2 started threatening plaintiff to implicate Sukhdev Sharma vs Kakpil Dev Sharma And Ors on 27 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79013699/ 2 him in false cases. On 21.05.2015, defendant no.1 finally left the suit property but defendant no.2 did not accompany defendant no.1 and she had no willingness to vacate the suit property. 2.3. Being aggrieved of acts and behavior of defendants, plaintiff and his wife also severed all their relations with the defendants vide newspaper publication dated 05.06.2015. The aforesaid publication was duly shown to defendant no. 2 by plaintiff and also requested defendant no. 2 to vacate the suit property and remove her belongings. However, instead of acceding to lawful requests of plaintiff and his wife, defendant no. 2 started quarreling with plaintiff and his wife on regular basis without any rhyme and reason. After defendant no. 1 left the suit property, he sometimes used to visit defendant no. 2 but never resided in the suit property. However, when defendant no. 1 came to know about the publication stated above, defendants in conspiracy with each other, got filed a petition under DV Act. Further, defendant no. 1 was also impleaded as one of the respondent in the said false and frivolous DV Act petition probably in order to remove any doubt qua conspiracies of defendants in filing the DV Act petition. Plaintiff and his wife have been impleaded as respondent no. 2 and 3 respectively in the said false and frivolous petition. The DV Act petition is in fact a counter blast against the public notice dated 05.06.2015 effected by plaintiff and his wife whereby all relations by plaintiff and his wife have been severed with defendants. 2.4. In above circumstances, plaintiff got served a notice upon defendant no. 2 to vacate the suit property and on service of the same, defendants through common relatives, requested 2-3 months time to arrange an accommodation and vacate the suit property, which time was granted by plaintiff. However, instead of vacating the suit property, defendants severed their harassment drive against plaintiff and his wife and now they are insisting upon plaintiff to sell the suit property and give share of defendant no. 1 to him. Since, the suit property is self acquired property of plaintiff by his own earnings, hence, defendant no. 1 has no share in the same and defendants were allowed by plaintiff to reside in the suit property only because of relationship. Intentions of defendants have gone malafide and they intend to pressurize plaintiff to accede to their unlawful demand of selling the suit property, as detailed above. 2.5. There are 3-4 covered almirahs in one of the walls of the bedroom in the suit property, wherein clothes and other articles of daily use are kept by plaintiff, his wife and defendant no. 2. Defendant no. 2 also causes hindrance for plaintiff and his wife in use of almirahs where clothes and other articles of plaintiff and his wife are kept/stored. The plaintiff has requested defendants number of times to not to behave in the aforesaid manner but all in vain. Plaintiff has also requested defendant no. 2 to vacate the suit property and remove her articles but she has been adamant and has not acceded to lawful requests of plaintiff even despite service of notice upon her. Plaintiff lastly requested defendants in last week of August 2016 to desist from indulging in nefarious activities, as detailed above, but to no avail. Similarly defendant no. 2 was also requested by plaintiff in last week of August 2016 to vacate the suit property and remove her articles from the area shown red in the site plan, but to no avail. 3 Upon service of summons of the suit, both defendants i.e., defendant no. 1 and defendant no. 2 filed the written statement to the suit of the plaintiff. The onus to prove both the issues was upon the plaintiff. The claim of the plaintiff rested on the premise that the plaintiff is the owner and in possession of the suit property and therefore seeks decree of mandatory injunction against defendant no. 2 to vacate the suit property and remove her articles/ belongings from the suit property and decree of permanent injunction against defendant no. 1 to restrain defendant no. 1 from entering the suit property. To prove its case, plaintiff has placed reliance upon copy of purported title documents, Ex. PW-1/3 (OSR) (Colly. 6 pages) and Ex. PW-1/4 (OSR) (Colly. 12 pages), copies of electricity bills Ex. PW-1/5 (Colly. 4 pages), copies of House Tax Receipts Ex.PW 1/6 (Colly. 11 pages) (OSR), copy of assessment order dated 06.01.1999 of MCD qua suit property Ex. PW 1/8 (OSR), copy of Notice dated 09.12.2014 of SDMC qua suit property Ex. PW -1/9 (OSR) and copy of Notice dated 26.03.2015 of SDMC qua suit property Ex. PW-1/10. 15.1.4 Defendant no. 1 who is stated to be the son of the plaintiff has not challenged the ownership of the plaintiff qua suit property. Defendant no. 2, however, has challenged the claim of the plaintiff with regard to the ownership of the suit property on the ground that the alleged property documents filed on behalf of plaintiff are not valid title deeds as the same are unregistered documents and the suit property was purchased out of the sale proceeds of ancestral property bearing no. J-10, Beriwala Bagh, Subash Nagar, Delhi (henceforth referred to as 'alleged ancestral property'). 15.1.5 The alleged ancestral property is in the name of wife of elder brother of the plaintiff. Since, the date of its purchase, plaintiff never had any right title or interest in the same. The alleged ancestral property was purchased by him somewhere in the year 1985-86 from one Sh. Tulsi Das for consideration of approximately Rs. 80,000/- out of which ground floor and first floor have already been sold by him to one Sh. Lucky around 20 years ago. On the second and third floor of the alleged ancestral property, PW 2 is residing with his two sons.
texts.arguments: Defendants have clearly told plaintiff that they will not accede to requests of plaintiff unless and until plaintiff gives them share of defendant no. 1 and on failure of plaintiff to do so, he and his wife will be further implicated in false and frivolous criminal cases. The plaintiff alleged that he requested defendants to vacate the suit property despite the fact Sukhdev Sharma vs Kakpil Dev Sharma And Ors on 27 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79013699/ 4 The plaintiff and his son in connivance with each other intentionally and deliberately cooked up false and baseless story just to defame the innocent defendant no. 2 after lapse of five years. 7.5. On the one hand defendant no. 2 submits that there is no restaurant or sweet shop in front portion of the suit property and on the other hand she alleges that the said restaurant and Sweet shop is being run jointly by plaintiff and defendant no. 1 and defendant no. 2 used to help them. 11.8. DW2 denied to the suggestions put by Ld. Counsel for plaintiff that the suit property was purchased by her father/plaintiff from his own funds; that her father never had any connection with property bearing no. J-10 Beriwala or same was owned by elder brother of her father; that all the allegations of harassment, cruelty and domestic violence made against the plaintiff and his wife are false and concocted; that the defendants are merely licensee in the suit property and they were permitted to reside in the same by the plaintiff. 11.9. DW2 when cross examined by Ld. Counsel for defendant no. 1 denied that she was told about the incidents of cruelty and domestic violence by defendant no. 2 and she never witnessed any such incidents (DW2 volunteered to depose that she had witnessed one such incident when Kapil Sharma was giving beatings to Ritu. She further deposed that she did not remember the exact date of the aforesaid incident of violence. She had reported the aforesaid incident to the police. She volunteered to depose that the aforesaid incident had occurred in the year 2015. Counsel for plaintiff deposed that she came to know about the alleged fact that the suit property is an ancestral property of the plaintiff from the family Sukhdev Sharma vs Kakpil Dev Sharma And Ors on 27 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79013699/ 14 members of the plaintiff i.e., plaintiff, his wife and her wife Pragati Sharma. The plaintiff in the reply to the written statement filed by defendant no. 2 has averred that the suit property was purchased by plaintiff from his own funds and the same is self acquired property of the plaintiff. As per para 4 of the case of 'Vinay Verma Vs. Kanika Pasricha and Anothers' decided on 29.11.2019 by Honble High Court of Delhi, (2019) 265 DLT 211, there are several categories of disputes which have arisen between parents/ in laws/ children. 15.1.20 The plaintiff has merely averred that instead of vacating the suit property, defendant severed their harassment drive against plaintiff and his wife and now they are insisting upon plaintiff to sell the suit property. It is further alleged that the DV Act petition is in fact a counter blast against a public notice dated 05.06.2015 effected by plaintiff and his wife whereby all relations by plaintiff and his wife have been severed with defendants. On the other hand, defendant no. 2 in her written statement has contended that the present suit has been filed in collusion with plaintiff, defendant no. 1 and their family members. The plaintiff in its plaint has averred that the plaintiff asked defendants to vacate the suit property number of times but to no avail. During the course of final arguments, Ld. Counsel for plaintiff relied heavily upon the case of Satish Chander Ahuja v. Sneha Ahuja, Civil Appeal No. 2483 of 2020, decided on 15.10.2020 by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India and in particular paragraph nos. 27, 43, 45, 79, 93, 95, 103, 104, 134, 106-116, 117, 25, 136 and 157. On the basis of the aforesaid judgment, it was argued by Ld. Counsel for plaintiff that the reliefs under Section 19 and 26 of DV Act can also be sought in Civil proceedings. The wife/ aggrieved person has to establish her right by pleadings and evidence and prove domestic violence in Civil Court to be entitled to any relief under Section 19 of DV Act in Civil Court. Section 17 of the DV Act provides that every woman in a domestic relationship shall have the right to reside in the shared household. Section 17 of DV Act reads as under: Right to reside in a shared household Sukhdev Sharma vs Kakpil Dev Sharma And Ors on 27 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79013699/ 21 (i)Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, every woman in a domestic relationship shall have the right to reside in the shared household, whether or not she has any right, title or beneficial interest in the same. (ii)The aggrieved person shall not be evicted or excluded from the shared household or any part of it by the respondent save in accordance with the procedure established by law. Section 26 of DV Act is reproduced herein below for reference: Relief in other suits and legal proceedings (I) Any relief available under sections 18, 19, 20, 21 and 22 may also be sought in any legal proceeding, before a civil Court, family Court or a criminal Court, affecting the aggrieved person and the respondent whether such proceeding was initiated before or after the commencement of this Act. (ii) Any relief referred to in sub-section (1) may be sought for in addition to and along with any other relief that the aggrieved person may seek in such suit or legal proceeding before a civil or criminal Court. (iii) In case any relief has been obtained by the aggrieved person in any proceedings other than a proceeding under this Act, she shall be bound to inform the Magistrate of the grant of such relief.
